title: Storyline spec
description: Single source of truth between the conversation and the renderer. Every mode writes the same spec; modes differ only in how far slides progress (status). The renderer turns it into a PPTX, and the source workbook is generated from data_points + sources.

mode.description: deck_detailed: slides reach status filled. deck_flow: slides stop at ghost (data_requirements filled, no values). deck_deep: a 30–60 slide deck built with the seven-step process; slides reach filled, and the spec also carries problem and issue_tree, from which sections, lead slides and evidence codes are built. single_slide: exactly one content slide; storyline.exec_summary has one item.

inputs.description: What the user gave us. Used for provenance: sources of kind user_provided point here.

issue_tree.description: Steps 2–6 of the seven-step process (deck_deep). Level-1 nodes (no parent) become the sections; kept leaves become the lead slide's index and the evidence codes (T-01…T-04).

data_points.description: Every number that appears on any slide. The source workbook has one sheet per slide built from these rows (rule A-07).

company_name.description: Shown where the footer brand goes (D8). Never 'McKinsey'.

theme.description: Color theme from templates/themes.json. Grammar is the same for every theme (D8).

font_pair.description: Overrides the theme's font pair. Omit to use the theme default (D10).

deck_type.description: deck_deep preset chosen at checkpoint 1. client_diagnostic: summary + contents tracker, sizing, ends on how to make it happen, appendix 15–30%. policy_analysis: methodology and sensitivities up front, appendix up to 55%. research_report: key questions or a framework as the agenda, ends on key takeaways (L-03, L-04).

content.description: Raw text, or a path for files.

governing_thought.description: The one-sentence answer the whole deck proves (G-04).

exec_summary.description: Each item is a lead message. Item ids become section ids and title prefixes (A-08). Reading only these must tell the whole story (B-04).

key_takeaways.description: Optional. Only when they say something the exec summary does not (B-05). Without them the end page shows next steps only.

supports.description: Content slide ids whose lead messages prove this bullet. QA: every exec item has ≥1, and every non-backup content slide is listed under exactly one item (B-04).

tracker_label.description: Short label for the auto-generated tracker (S3).

tree_node.description: deck_deep: the level-1 issue_tree node this section answers (T-01).

lead_slide.description: deck_deep: the content slide right after the divider that states the section's answer and indexes its leaves (numbered-levers, framework or table; L-01).

parent_id.description: Sub-section of this section (sections over ~20 pages, L-02). Shares its parent's exec_item_id.

question.description: deck_deep: the question this section answers, listed on the Key questions page (china27 form).

role.description: agenda_tracker: contents page; with section_id it is repeated before that section with the section emphasised. section_divider: section opener (needs section_id); lead_message.text overrides the section's exec summary claim. problem_statement (deck_deep): 'Key questions', drawn from spec.problem and each section's question; not a content slide, so it needs no exec item. appendix_divider: opens the appendix and lists every backup page (R9); the agenda then ends with an Appendix row.

parent_id.description: Overview slide that assigned this slide's id (S2).

backup_of.description: For role backup: the content slide this supports. Title gets the 'BACKUP:' prefix (S4). deck_deep: the 'what we did not pursue' slide sets tree_node (the pruned nodes) instead.

tree_node.description: deck_deep: the issue_tree leaf this evidence slide proves (its code is the title prefix, T-02). On the appendix 'what we did not pursue' slide: the pruned node(s) it lists.

status.description: ghost = lead message + archetype + data_requirements, no values (flow mode end state). drafted = body written, some placeholders. filled = every number has a data_ref with a source. qa_passed = all QA rules pass.

unit_line.description: '**Metric**, unit, period' under the title. Required on chart slides (A-06).

sticker.description: Set to 'ILLUSTRATIVE — DATA NEEDED' automatically when any point on the slide is a placeholder (L3).

data_requirements.description: What data would prove the lead message. Written in every mode; it is the only body content in flow mode.

rationale.description: Why this archetype was chosen (routing table row). Shown to the user, not rendered.

so_what.description: Optional one-sentence conclusion shown at the bottom of the body (A-12). The action title stays the main conclusion (B-01); use this on some slides, not all.

so_what_style.description: bar = dark full-width bar; line = thin rule + accent bar + bold sentence (lighter). No label: public decks never print 'So what'.

callout.description: Small highlighted box attached to the one element the title points at (A-02). target = the element's header, label or id (column, table row, process step, framework item, lever code).

basis.description: How an estimate on this slide was built (B-08), drawn as a strip of number cards under the exhibit.

text.description: So-what sentence, ≤2 rendered lines, ~10–20 words, no trailing period (B-01, A-03, D8).

prefix.description: Tracker code like '2a:' or 'Example:' or 'BACKUP:'. Rendered before text; generated from ids when omitted.

numbers.description: Numbers that appear in the title, each tied to the data point that shows it on the slide (A-01).

text.description: As written in the title, e.g. '2x', '$120M', '~40%'.

highlights.description: Items the title names; only these get the accent color (A-02).

count_word.description: 'Three drivers' → 3; must equal the number of body elements (A-04).

is_question.description: If true, the answer must sit in a callout or sidebar (routing rule R3).

archetype.description: Tier 1 (20) first, then Tier 2, then navigation. See docs/archetypes/README.md.

sidebar.description: Right third, joined to the body by a chevron (L4, B-02: evidence left, conclusion right).

reasons.description: Numbered reasons (e.g. why the focus quadrant wins). Each has a takeaway header and a one-line detail.

note.description: Short line at the bottom of the sidebar, e.g. the next step.

rows.description: Label + value rows with a small bar, under the big number or bullets. Fills the sidebar with sourced numbers (A-12).

basis.description: How the row's estimate was calculated, e.g. '16% of sales × 26% share' (B-08). Shown under the label.

implication.description: What the exhibit means for us, in its own box at the foot of the sidebar. Use it instead of a 'For us:' bullet.

implication_style.description: Leave it out: the renderer rotates dark box, rule, accent bar and circled '!' in deck order, so neighbouring slides differ. Set it only to force one look on a slide.

point.description: A value shown on a slide. Either it references a data point (filled), or it is a placeholder (ghost or drafted). A literal value without data_ref is invalid (D5).

placeholder.description: Rendered as a dashed '?' mark plus the sticker.

points.description: Same length and order as categories.

role.description: primary | comparator | forecast. Not drawn differently yet; forecasts are labeled in the categories (e.g. 2027E).

series.description: Category charts: one series per legend entry. scatter: series[0] = x values, series[1] = y values, optional series[2] = bubble sizes; categories name the points.

sort.description: C1: desc unless order carries meaning (time, geography).

highlight.description: Categories to accent; must match lead_message.highlights (A-02).

waterfall_steps.description: For chart_type waterfall: which categories are start/end totals vs. steps.

x_format.description: scatter: number format of the x axis (value_format is the y axis).

reference_lines.description: scatter: dashed average lines that split the plot into four areas.

quadrant_labels.description: scatter: names of the four areas made by the average lines, in order top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right (empty string = no name).

label_points.description: scatter: which points carry their name. Default all up to 14 points, else highlighted only.

relation.description: One line comparing the number to a benchmark, e.g. '2.4x the market average of 5.5%'. Numbers here need their own data_ref in the slide.

drivers.description: What drives the number (filled) or what is missing (placeholder). 2–4 lines.

drivers_header.description: Optional label over the driver lines ('Why it matters', 'Behind the number'). Without it a thin rule separates them; avoid the same label on every KPI slide.

panels.description: All panels prove the same lead message (B-03). Each header is a takeaway sentence (B-02).

connector.description: Arrow between panels only when the left panel causes or leads to the right one (B-09). Parallel evidence: none.

badge.description: Row id; becomes a tracker prefix on later slides (S2).

note.description: Short verdict for the row. With a slide callout, every row's note is shown in a right-hand column; the callout target row is highlighted.

benchmark.description: heatmap: a reference row (e.g. peer median), shown plain and left out of the shading. Put it first.

verdict_header.description: Header of the verdict column, which holds row notes and the callout (default 'Verdict').

low_is_better.description: heatmap: columns where a lower value is better; their shading is inverted so darker always means better.

header.description: Leads with the takeaway of this box (B-02).

point_caption.description: Label for the item's number, e.g. 'Margin impact by 2027'.

footer.description: One bold line at the bottom of the box, e.g. owner and start date, or the exit gate of a step.

from_to.description: Render as From → To columns instead of chevrons.

mece_note.description: How the branches are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (G-03).

operator.description: How the children combine into this node.

statement.description: archetype 'statement': the lead message itself is set large in the middle of the slide. No chart, no bullets.

support.description: Optional one-line support under the statement (B-02: point first, then detail).

emphasis.description: Phrases of the statement shown in the accent color. Must appear in lead_message.text (A-02).

split.description: Split variant: statement on a solid accent panel on the left, support on the right.

quotes.description: archetype 'quote-interview': quote cards. Quotes are verbatim; **phrase** marks the words the title rests on.

text.description: Verbatim quote, no quotation marks. With placeholder: true, what the quote needs to show.

speaker.description: Role and organization type, never a private person's name (e.g. 'Head of procurement, regional grocer').

emphasis.description: The card the title points at.

source_id.description: Interview notes or survey the quote comes from (A-07).

placeholder.description: Not a quote yet (ghost or drafted): text says what quote is needed, speaker says from whom. Drawn as a dashed 'Quote needed' card, never as a quote.

metric.description: What the number measures, shown under it, e.g. 'of shoppers say it is hard to find' (B-10).

headers.description: Column headers: [moves column, numbers column], e.g. ['Move', 'Evidence']. Required when items carry numbers (B-10).

situation_header.description: Takeaway header for the situation column (B-02). Default 'Situation'.

approach_header.description: Takeaway header for the approach column (B-02). Default 'Approach'.

connector.description: Arrows between columns (B-09). Default: only before Impact, since situation and approach are not cause and effect.

description.description: e.g. 'Share of firms using gen AI in production, by sector, US, 2025'.

recommended_exhibit.description: e.g. 'Sorted horizontal bar, software highlighted, average row last'.

candidate_sources.description: Where to look: user files first (D2), then named public sources.

data_point.description: One row in the source workbook: Data point | Value | Source | URL | Excerpt | Accessed | Used in.

slide_id.description: First slide that shows this number. Reuse the same data point on later slides instead of copying it.

excerpt.description: Verbatim text or table cell the value was taken from.

locator.description: Page, table or cell in the source.

derived_from.description: For source kind derived: inputs to the calculation.

used_in.description: Which slide element shows it, e.g. 'bar: Software', 'title', 'sidebar'.

value_high.description: Upper end of a range (value = lower end). Shown as e.g. '4–5 years'.

calc.description: Machine-readable formula over data point ids, e.g. '(us1 - pl1) * 100'. Becomes a live Excel formula; check.py recomputes it (B-08).

estimate.description: true for projections, sizings and uplifts: our own estimate, not a fact. Needs calc, assumptions and a visible basis on the slide (B-08).

assumptions.description: Every assumption behind an estimate, one per line. Listed in the Calculations sheet.

geography.description: Where the number applies (country, state, market), when the source covers more than one (V-02).

definition.description: What exactly is counted when the label could mean more than one thing, e.g. 'nominal USD, calendar year, employer firms only' (V-02).

verified.description: Second-pass re-check (V-05): the page was opened again before rendering and the excerpt looked for. verify.py writes it; a verifier or the user may override it after reading the page.

corroboration.description: Second independent sources for the same number (V-06): required for title and exec summary numbers in deck_deep. A value that differs needs a note saying which one is used and why.

kind.description: D2: user_provided wins when it conflicts with web.

name.description: As printed on the slide's 'Source:' line.

input_id.description: For user_provided: which input it came from.

tier.description: Web sources (V-03). T1 primary: official statistics, regulators, filings, peer-reviewed papers, the company's own disclosures about itself. T2 established research firms, industry bodies, reputable surveys. T3 reporting on another source (news, summaries): trace to the primary. T4 not citable for numbers: blogs, vendor marketing about the market, SEO aggregators, AI-generated pages.

cites.description: T3 only: the primary source the report relies on, if it could not be reached.

recency_ok.description: Why a source published 4+ years ago still holds (V-04), e.g. 'latest edition; census runs every 5 years'.

op.description: Operator shown before this term. The last term is the result and takes '='.

caption.description: What the number is, in plain words (B-10). Add the source if it is not ours: '(supplier review, 2025)'.

body_equation.description: A calculation drawn as number cards joined by operators (B-08). Use it when the slide's point is how an estimate is built.

problem.description: Step 1 problem definition worksheet and the step 4 one-day answer (P-01). Shown on the 'question we were asked' slide and used for the closing check.

statement.description: One sentence: outcome-focused, specific and measurable, time-bound, set at the highest level the decision maker owns. A question, not a topic.

decision_maker.description: Who decides and what they will decide.

success_criteria.description: How the decision maker will judge the answer (a number, a threshold, a yes/no).

accuracy.description: Precision the decision needs ('order of magnitude', '±10%').

out_of_scope.description: Boundaries and off-limits options agreed at checkpoint 1.

one_day_answer.description: Best answer before the analysis, in exactly three parts (situation · observation/complication · resolution).

issue_node.description: One node of the hypothesis tree. A node without parent is a level-1 branch (= a section); a node no other node names as parent is a leaf.

code.description: Index code: '2' for a branch, '2a' for its leaf. Evidence titles start with it ('2a:', T-02). Required on every kept node.

label.description: Short name for trackers and the lead slide index ('Demand').

hypothesis.description: A testable sentence, not a label ('Mid-market firms will pay for AP automation within 2 years').

priority.description: Step 3: how much the answer depends on it × whether the decision maker can move it.

cut_reason.description: Set when the branch is pruned. Pruned branches go to the appendix 'what we did not pursue' slide (T-02).

workplan.description: Step 4: the analysis that would prove or kill the hypothesis.

exhibit.description: Dummied chart: archetype or chart type and axes.

knock_out.description: An analysis that could end the branch on its own; run these first.

finding.description: Step 5–6 result. refuted and revised leaves get new titles (T-04).

body_cost_curve.description: Cost curve (archetype cost-curve): one bar per measure, width = volume, height = unit cost, sorted from cheapest; bars below zero save money. Drawn as shapes (native charts cannot vary bar width).

group.description: Colour group, shown in the legend (max 4 groups).

x_label.description: '**Metric**, unit', bottom right, e.g. '**Hours saved a month**, per customer, cumulative'.

price_line.description: Dashed horizontal line, e.g. a carbon price or the plan uplift.

bracket.description: Brace over a run of bars with a pill value; must equal the title number (A-01).

tail.description: Grey block closing the curve: volume with no measure yet ('TBD').

highlight.description: Bars the title names; they get the accent colour.

body_org.description: Org chart (archetype org-chart): same-size boxes per level, elbow connectors, roles in callouts outside the boxes, new units filled dark with a legend.

label.description: Unit or role name, 6 words at most.

sub.description: One short line under the label.

count.description: Shown as stacked copies: one per region or team.

dotted.description: Dotted line to the parent (advisory or indirect).

side.description: Committees outside the hierarchy, drawn as an oval beside the node they advise.

roles.description: 'Key roles' callouts tied to a node; role text never goes inside the boxes.

body_initiative.description: Initiative one-pager (archetype initiative-one-pager). One template per deck; the title starts with the initiative's code.

header.description: actions_impact: the initiative's one-line aim, in the band under the title.

impact.description: actions_impact: the row's expected result, shown in a right-hand column. Give a point when it is a number (it needs a data point like any other).

description.description: description_case and pros_prereqs: what the initiative is.

impact.description: Pulled-out impact pill (never buried in the text).

result_header.description: Header of the result column (default 'Expected result').

body_map.description: Map (archetype map), drawn from Natural Earth outlines as editable shapes. World: Miller projection without Antarctica; US: Albers with Alaska and Hawaii insets.

geo.description: world: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes. us_states: USPS codes (50 states and DC).

style.description: choropleth: regions shaded in 4–6 steps of one hue. highlight: a few regions in 1–3 accent groups on grey. bubble: circles at region centres, area proportional to value.

extent.description: auto: the whole geography. The others crop a world map.

regions.description: choropleth and bubble: one entry per region with a value. A listed region without a value, or an unlisted one, is drawn as No data.

breaks.description: choropleth: class edges in the data's units (fractions for %), ascending; 3–5 edges give 4–6 classes. Omit to let the renderer pick round edges.

groups.description: highlight: accent groups, shown in the legend.

callouts.description: Notes in aligned edge columns, joined to the region by an elbow leader line.

body_marimekko.description: Marimekko (archetype marimekko): variable-width 100% columns, no y axis; column width = its share, cells = shares within the column. Drawn as shapes. Pair it with a takeaway sidebar.

rows.description: Row names, top to bottom, labelled once at the left (no legend).

cells.description: One point per row, in row order; shares of the column summing to 100%.

width_label.description: What the column widths measure, under the chart.

highlight.description: Cells outlined in the accent colour.

body_donut.description: Donuts (archetype donut): 1–4 equal-size rings, the share in accent from 12 o'clock clockwise, the rest grey, the value in the centre.

emphasis.description: Ring in the primary colour instead of the accent.

detail.description: 2–3 short lines under the donut: what drives the share.

body_landscape.description: Landscape (archetype landscape): segments as equal columns of name chips (no logos).

note.description: One bold line under the column: what the segment shows.

marked.description: Names outlined and bold (e.g. players that already ship the feature).

marked_label.description: What the outline means, shown in the key.

us.description: Our company's name, filled in the accent colour.

body_from_to.description: From–to shift (archetype from-to): two parallel columns, the To side stronger, one arrow between the headers.

label.description: Optional dimension name in a left column ('Data entry').

to_detail.description: One line under the To headline: how or why.

body_venn.description: Venn (archetype venn): 2–3 translucent circles of one hue; the overlaps stay unlabelled except the centre, explained in a notes column.

centre.description: What sits where all sets meet; the notes column's header.
